stress.pt.not_enough: Not enough pre-treatment periods or groups to test pre-trends.
stress.pt.plausible: Parallel trends: plausible. No evidence of differential pre-treatment trends (p = {p:.3f}).
stress.pt.questionable: Parallel trends: questionable. The joint test of pre-treatment group-specific trends rejects equal trends (p = {p:.3f}); differential pre-trends threaten the parallel-trends assumption.
stress.pt.violated: Parallel trends: violated. The joint test of pre-treatment group-specific trends rejects equal trends (p = {p:.3f}); differential pre-trends threaten the parallel-trends assumption.
stress.anticipation.not_enough: Not enough data to test for anticipation effects.
stress.anticipation.warning: Outcome jumps for treated units in the period right before treatment (p = {p:.3f}), suggesting possible anticipation.
stress.anticipation.pass: No evidence of anticipatory behavior just before treatment (p = {p:.3f}).
stress.spillovers.non_numeric: Unit identifiers are not numeric, so no neighbourhood structure is available to test for spillovers.
stress.spillovers.too_few: Too few adjacent / non-adjacent control units to test for spillovers; default pass.
stress.spillovers.warning: The {n} control unit(s) adjacent to a treated unit shift by {effect:+.3f} after treatment relative to other controls (p = {p:.3f}). Spillovers contaminate the comparison group.
stress.spillovers.pass: Control units adjacent to a treated unit do not change differently after treatment (difference = {effect:+.3f}, p = {p:.3f}).
stress.serial.warning: Within-unit Durbin-Watson statistic = {dw:.2f}; implied residual autocorrelation (corrected for fixed-effects bias) = {rho:.2f}. Serially correlated errors make non-clustered standard errors too small (Bertrand, Duflo & Mullainathan 2004): keep clustering by unit, and consider a wild-cluster bootstrap when clusters are few.
stress.serial.pass: Within-unit Durbin-Watson statistic = {dw:.2f}; implied residual autocorrelation (corrected for fixed-effects bias) = {rho:.2f}, no strong evidence of serial correlation.
stress.heterogeneity.too_few: Too few treated or control units to assess effect heterogeneity; default pass.
stress.heterogeneity.warning: Pre/post changes vary more across treated units than across controls (variance ratio = {ratio:.2f}, p = {p:.3f}). A single average treatment effect may mask important heterogeneity.
stress.heterogeneity.pass: Pre/post changes are no more dispersed across treated units than across controls (variance ratio = {ratio:.2f}, p = {p:.3f}).
rec.did.intro: Difference-in-Differences is potentially appropriate because treatment occurs at a defined point in time and the data contain treated and comparison units observed before and after the intervention.
rec.did.staggered: Treatment adoption is staggered: a standard two-way fixed-effects DiD estimate can be contaminated by already-treated units used as controls. A heterogeneity-robust estimator (Callaway & Sant'Anna, de Chaisemartin & D'Haultfoeuille) is recommended over the canonical TWFE specification.
rec.did.spillovers: Because nearby or related units may also be affected (spillovers), a Spatial Spillover Analysis extension is recommended alongside the baseline DiD.
rec.did.assumption: Parallel trends between treated and comparison units in the absence of treatment.
rec.event_study.intro: An Event Study is a natural extension of DiD: it estimates period-by-period treatment effects and lets you inspect pre-treatment coefficients directly as an informal test of the parallel-trends assumption.
rec.event_study.few_pre: Fewer than two pre-treatment periods are available, which limits the ability to visually or statistically assess pre-trends.
rec.event_study.assumption: No anticipation effects; parallel trends in each pre-treatment period.
rec.event_study.concern: Statistical power in periods far from the treatment date.
rec.synthetic_control.intro: Synthetic Control is most useful when a single (or very few) treated unit(s) can be compared against a weighted combination of untreated donor units that closely tracks its pre-treatment trajectory.
rec.synthetic_control.assumption: No interference between the treated unit and donor units; good pre-treatment fit.
rec.synthetic_control.concern: Inference relies on placebo-based permutation tests rather than standard errors.
rec.iv.intro: Instrumental Variables can address endogenous treatment assignment, but the score here is capped because no valid instrument has been declared in the current project — relevance and exclusion restriction cannot be assessed automatically.
rec.iv.assumption: Instrument relevance and exclusion restriction (no direct effect on the outcome).
rec.iv.concern: Weak instruments bias estimates toward the OLS estimate.
rec.rdd.matches: Regression Discontinuity is only appropriate when treatment is assigned by whether a running variable crosses a known cutoff. This design's assignment mechanism is '{mechanism}', which matches this requirement.
rec.rdd.no_match: Regression Discontinuity is only appropriate when treatment is assigned by whether a running variable crosses a known cutoff. This design's assignment mechanism is '{mechanism}', which does not obviously match this requirement.
rec.rdd.assumption: No manipulation of the running variable around the cutoff.
rec.rdd.concern: Local validity only: estimates apply near the cutoff, not to the full population.
rec.matching.intro: Matching / propensity-score methods require that, conditional on observed covariates, treatment assignment is as good as random (no unobserved confounding). This is a strong and untestable assumption.
rec.matching.concern: Unobserved confounding cannot be ruled out or tested directly.
rec.rct.declared: A Randomized Controlled Trial design was declared for this project.
rec.rct.not_declared: A Randomized Controlled Trial design was not declared for this project: treatment assignment is described as non-random, so an RCT-style analysis is not applicable retroactively. This score reflects that an RCT was not the assignment mechanism used.
diagnosis.note.staggered: Staggered treatment timing detected: standard two-way fixed-effects DiD can be biased under treatment-effect heterogeneity (Goodman-Bacon 2021; de Chaisemartin & D'Haultfoeuille 2020). Consider heterogeneity-robust DiD estimators.
diagnosis.note.endogenous_language: The research question mentions self-selection or reverse causality language; treat the assignment mechanism as potentially endogenous.
diagnosis.note.no_pre_periods: No pre-treatment periods are available: pre-trends and time-invariant confounding cannot be assessed directly.
diagnosis.note.spatial: Spatial or network language detected: treated and comparison units may not be independent (SUTVA violation). Consider a spillover / spatial-DiD analysis.

warn.weak_instrument: Weak instrument: first-stage F = {f:.1f} < {threshold:.0f}. 2SLS is biased toward OLS and its confidence interval is unreliable.
warn.overlap: Overlap: {n} treated observation(s) have a propensity score outside the range of control propensity scores; their matches are poor.
warn.imbalance_after_matching: Some covariates remain imbalanced after matching (|standardized difference| > 0.1).

warn.sc_convergence: The weight optimizer did not report convergence; weights may be slightly suboptimal.
warn.sc_fit: Poor pre-treatment fit: RMSPE = {rmspe:.3f}, more than half the treated unit's pre-treatment outcome SD. The treated unit may lie outside the donors' convex hull.

model.downs.name: Downsian median voter
model.downs.description: Two office-seeking parties choose platforms on a line; voters with single-peaked preferences vote for the closer platform. Both parties converge to the median voter's ideal point.
model.probabilistic_voting.name: Probabilistic voting
model.probabilistic_voting.description: Parties maximize expected vote share when voters' choices are subject to random ideological shocks. Policy converges to an average of group ideal points weighted by group size and responsiveness: responsive (swing) groups get more weight.
model.tullock.name: Tullock rent-seeking contest ({n} contestants)
model.tullock.description: Interest groups spend resources to win a politically allocated rent; each wins with probability proportional to its effort. With identical prizes each spends (n-1)V/n^2 and a share (n-1)/n of the rent is dissipated.
model.niskanen.name: Niskanen budget-maximizing bureau
model.niskanen.description: A bureau with a monopoly on supply maximizes its budget subject to covering its costs. When budget-constrained it produces twice the socially optimal output.
model.public_good.name: Voluntary public-good provision ({n} contributors)
model.public_good.description: Citizens split their income between private consumption and contributions to a public good. Free riding leads to under-provision; poorer citizens may not contribute at all.
model.cournot.name: Cournot oligopoly ({n} firms)
model.cournot.description: Firms choose quantities simultaneously facing linear inverse demand P = a - bQ.
model.bertrand.name: Bertrand duopoly with differentiated products
model.bertrand.description: Two firms set prices for imperfect substitutes with linear demands q_i = a - b p_i + d p_j.
param.downs.m: Median voter's ideal point (one-dimensional policy space)
param.tullock.prize: Value of the rent (prize) for contestant {i}
param.niskanen.a: Sponsor's marginal valuation at zero output
param.public_good.alpha: Weight on private consumption (1 - alpha on the public good)

methods.assumption.rct: Treatment is randomly assigned, so treated and control groups are comparable in expectation on observed and unobserved characteristics.
methods.assumption.matching: Selection on observables: conditional on the covariates, treatment is as good as random, and every treated unit has comparable controls (overlap).
methods.assumption.iv: The instrument moves the treatment (relevance) and affects the outcome only through the treatment (exclusion). Exclusion cannot be tested from the data.
methods.assumption.rdd: Treatment switches on when the running variable crosses a known cutoff, and units cannot precisely manipulate which side they fall on; everything else varies smoothly at the cutoff.
methods.assumption.synthetic_control: Before treatment, a weighted average of untreated donor units reproduces the treated unit's outcome path, and donors are not affected by the treatment.
methods.assumption.dml: All confounders are observed among the covariates (unconfoundedness), possibly acting non-linearly; the treatment effect is constant (partially linear model).
methods.need_running: Running variable: select a numeric column to set the cutoff.
methods.need_unit_period: Unit / Period: select both columns to choose the treated unit and period.
